scope: Non-null LFS/LGS under explicit KernelEventsNoFaultV6, Intel 16/32/64-bit operand rules

references.manual: AMD APM volume 2, 24593 revision 3.44, section 4.5.3, processor-dependent null-selector policy

native_oracle.host: Intel Core i9-13900H, Linux x64 KVM
compared: 32 additional bytes spanning the high virtual source alias in wrap cases
coverage: all 16 GPR destinations with 16-bit preservation and 32-bit zero extension
GDT and LDT including LDT entry zero
conforming code and all admitted DPL/RPL combinations
base, expanded limit, attributes and unusable-bit installation
accessed-bit aliasing into the offset or selector field
all base/index registers, scales, RIP/EIP and no-base SIB addressing
old FS/GS bases, including when loading the same segment
independent addr32 field wrapping before 64-bit segment addition
exact original fallthrough, flags and NMI blocking

checks.ordinary_contracts: original undefined-independence certificate and ordinary source both refused; no residual publication
checks.sdk_driver: HighC/LLVMC O0/O2 with ASan/UBSan: coupled destinations, cache fields, budgets, exact fallthrough and atomic null-selector rejection
checks.format_and_docs: pinned clang-format and localized Markdown/link checks

discovered_and_fixed.issue: addr32 computes the selector field effective address modulo 2^32 before segment addition; a contiguous linear image approximation is incorrect at wrap
discovered_and_fixed.observation: 67 65 49 0F B5 04 25 F9 FF FF FF at PC 0x1250, GS.base=0xffffffff00008807, offset linear address 0x8800, selector fault at 0xffffffff00008808
discovered_and_fixed.qualification: A high virtual alias at 4 GiB keeps both fields mapped and checks all three widths and both segments against independent original instructions; the final tests all pass.

limitations: CPL0 long-mode entry, Intel operand-size rules and successful sequential ordinary RAM
null selectors need an explicit processor-specific base policy and are rejected before descriptor access or any write
LSS interrupt/debug inhibition and i386/compatibility LDS/LES/LFS/LGS/LSS remain open
fault delivery, MMIO, concurrent writers, CET/FRED and asynchronous events remain outside the profile
ordinary strict/permissive lifting and native proofs retain their refusal
global x86 gaps and NeverC full-CI qualification remain open; no LLVM release or pin change
